Question: What are the trickiest questions asked in an interview?
Answer: Was asked this one recently. Many of you might know the answer. I did not. Interviewer: Suppose you have 9 rubber balls out of which 8 have the same weight and 1 is heavier than the rest. Given 2 tries and a weighing scale (2 pan beam scale), how would you find out which one is the heaviest? I scribbled on paper for about 5 minutes. Had this fear of rejection constantly pooling my mind. Had to give an answer, even though a lame one, but some answer. Me: OK. I will drop all 9 balls on the ground from the same height. The one which bounces the least will be the heaviest (Not a generic answer, but better than saying 'I don't know'). Interviewer (shocked by my answer): That's a scientific answer. Me: Yes, but it's an answer, right? Interviewer: How will you ensure that the balls are dropped from the same height? The force can be different. And what if the ground is uneven or has carpet on it? None of the balls will bounce right? Me: Releasing balls from the same height ensures that the force is the same. I will place the weighing scale pan on the ground. Will drop 5 balls on the pan. Mark the lowest bounce from that batch. Will then drop the remaining 4 balls and repeat the same. Now the lowest bounce from the 2 batches is the heaviest ball. Interviewer: OK. Cool. I admit my answer wasn't the correct one. But no matter what, you should at least try and speak your mind. All such questions portray how well you react during stressful situations at job. I was SELECTED. But I rejected the offer due to some reasons. The answer I found on Google (not even close to my answer): Simple, right? :)
